title: 还清房贷十年后：催债信突然上门，华尔街如何从旧债中获利？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Our parents never own their own homes, so we jumped at the idea of following that American
segments.zh: 我们的父母从未拥有自己的房子，所以我们很向往那个美国梦，想在自己的房子里养大孩子。

segments.en: dream and raising our kids in our own home.
segments.zh: 大多数美国人通过房屋净值来积累财富和构建财务未来。

segments.en: The majority of people in the United States build their wealth and their financial future with the equity of their home.
segments.zh: 一个消费者噩梦正变得越来越真实，成千上万的房主深受其害。

segments.en: A consumer horror story that's becoming all too real for thousands of homeowners.
segments.zh: 这些僵尸抵押贷款正在剥夺人们的房屋净值。

segments.en: And these zombie mortgages are robbing people of the equity.
segments.zh: 他们以为早已还清的贷款，实际上又回来纠缠他们，有些人甚至面临流落街头的风险。

segments.en: Mortgages that they thought were paid off a long time ago were actually coming back to haunt them, putting some at risk of ending up on the street.
segments.zh: 我们知道，这类贷款还有数万甚至数十万笔挂在账上。

segments.en: We know it's tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of these loans are still out there on the books.
segments.zh: 这是一门利润极其丰厚的生意。

segments.en: This is a hugely profitable business.
segments.zh: 我们之所以报道这个故事，部分原因是拿到了某家私募股权公司的记录。

segments.en: We came to this story in part because we got records on one particular private equity firm.
We called them the foreclosure files.
And we decided that we had a unique chance to really get inside this business and figure out how it operated.
segments.zh: 我们觉得这是个难得的机会，可以深入了解这个行业，弄清它的运作方式。

segments.en: We can see how much money people are making.
segments.zh: 我们能看到人们赚了多少钱。
